AGENDA
  YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Tuesday, June 22, 2021
  6:30 P.M.
  The three-fold mission of the Youth & Family Action Committee is:
  1. To support positive activities and opportunities for young people;
  2. To strengthen families; and
  3. To combat the problems of substance abuse.

Tonight’s meeting will be held virtually in compliance with Governor Newson’s Executive
Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. The meeting will be live streamed on
the La Verne You Tube channel at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream.

To make a comment on an agenda item or under public comment, email your phone
number to cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. This email address will be monitored live during the
meeting and interested parties will be called. Please be aware there is a delay in the live
stream service and any requests to speak should be submitted as soon as possible.

minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  June 22, 2021

1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present (virtually):

  Executive Board
  Robin Carder, Chair – Council Member
  Rick Crosby, Vice Chair – Council Member
  Krista Chakman, BUSD Board Member
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Don Kendrick, Resident
  Donna Redman, Resident
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Janessa Gonzalez, LVPD
  Chad Peterson, City of La Verne
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Assoc.
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the March 23, 2021, meeting were
  approved.

4. Teen Center Design  Community Services Supervisor Chad Peterson
  provided an overview of the various design phases of
  the proposed Teen Center. The different designs
  represent changes after receiving feedback from the
  community. Chad also updated the group on the
  status of the grant application to support
  construction.

5. City Youth Programs  Chad handled this item as well and updated the
  group for what activities have been available noting
  that a majority of the regular programs weren’t able
  to go forward the last several months. However, with
  the relaxation of the County Health Guidelines, more
  programs are coming on line especially as it relates
  to outside program. Chad noted that some of the
  program sign-ups are a little lower but others are
  attracting many participants.

  Chad also shared information regarding the
  upcoming 4th of July festivities in town.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes June 22, 2021, page 2

6. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer Janessa Gonzalez provided
  a report to the group. Janessa noted that students
  back on campus was welcome and that they were
  well behaved. Janessa also shared information
  about the various successful graduations and
  anticipation of getting ready for a more normal school
  year next year.

  Lieutenant Gonzalez also explained Janessa’s role
  during the summer and the excellent job she is doing
  for the City.

7. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with the Bonita Unified School District
  shared input on the challenges associated with high
  school sports and overcoming those with constant
  changes to guidelines. Mark shared perspective of
  how restrictive things were in the beginning and then
  how they progressed to near normal activities. Mark
  noted that there were many successful
  accomplishments throughout the challenging journey.

  Vice Chair Crosby thanked the BUSD and staff’s effort
  to provide a sense of normalcy back to the community.
  BUSD Chair Chakmak provided information about
  summer school and shared information about
  recognizing first responders who had recently saved
  the life of a high school coach.

  Lastly the group discussed the potential masking
  requirements for the next school year.

8. Tobacco Ordinance  JR Ranells with the City provided a history of YFAC’s
  direction for the Police Department to work with
  Jessica Vozella and the American Lung Association to
  draft a Tobacco Ordinance banning all flavored
  tobacco products. There will be an exception in regard
  to menthol products related to legal challenges. The
  group discussed the specifics and what is included. It
  is anticipated that the draft ordinance will go before the
  City Council for consideration at the July 19th meeting.

  Jessica noted that she was very excited La Verne is
  taking this significant step forward. Jessica also noted
  that menthol remains a significant public health issue
  and encouraged the group to be diligent in protecting
  the community. Sam shared that the City is keeping
  menthol’s on its radar in anticipation that the ordinance
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes June 22, 2021, page 3

  can eventually be amended once there is less of a
  legal concern.

9. Public Comment  Jason Lorge thanked everyone for their work on behalf
  of the community.

  Robin requested the group to share any potential
  agenda items for future consideration.

  Krista inquired and shared a desire for the next
  meeting to be in person. It wasn’t yet known if the
  next meeting would be in person.

10. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for July 27th at
  6:30 p.m.

11. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:15 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Assistant to the City Manager
